subject: Private release: safety raft & undo protocol — proposed cadence and windows
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Ben Harris <ben.harris@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Private release: safety raft & undo protocol — proposed cadence and windows

Team, Ben — attaching a short proposal for how we want to run the upcoming Private maintenance (version bump + security hotpatch) for AcmeHealth. This is intentionally more operational than the standard pin/rollback doc: I want explicit "safety raft" lanes (fast undo, staged canary, and full evacuation) and clear ownership for each lane.

High-level proposal (TL;DR):
- Maintenance cadence: two-stage release (canary day + broad day) spread across two maintenance windows: 02:00-05:00 local (customer) on Tue (canary) and Wed (broad).
- Pinning: pin cluster to release X.Y.Z at T0 for canary nodes; allow auto-unpin after 72h if no regressions.
- Undo lanes (safety raft):
  1) Fast undo (minutes): revert routing / traffic weights to previous model variant using runtime router — no node reboots.
  2) Staged rollback (30–90m): drain affected pool, redeploy previous image to canary subset, validate KV/cache warmup.
  3) Evacuation (hours): cordon and move customer traffic to fallback dedicated pool or hosted fallback model.
- Gating metrics: 95th latency, token drop errors, OOM/eviction rate, and model-quality alerts from evaluation harness. If any gating metric breaches threshold during canary, automatically stop rollout and trigger staged rollback.
- Network considerations: pre-schedule egress firewall exception windows for our staging agents and ensure our BGP maintenance windows are coordinated with Acme ops.
- Testing: mirror 10% traffic to canary for 2 hours before full cutover; run KV cache warmup script as part of post-deploy hook.

Preflight checklist (short):
- Signed maintenance window (customer + infra team) — we have Ben's verbal ok, need written confirmation.
- Updated pin TTL and a documented auto-unpin path.
- Doc links and runbook: see attached safety-raft PDF + checklist spreadsheet.
- Oncall & escalation list: list below.

Escalation points (primary):
- Stephanie Nguyen (release lead) — +1 (415) 555-0192
- Dev Patel (runtime) — dev@redwood.ai
- Laura Bennett (customer ops) — laura@redwood.ai

Open questions for the thread:
1) Dev — does the KV-cache warmup script require special coordination with the orchestrator (drain timing)?
2) Laura — are the proposed windows workable for Acme's DB maintenance schedule?
3) Ben — are there egress constraints / firewall approvers we should add to the ticket?

Attaching: redwood-safety-raft-v1.pdf (high-level matrix) and preflight-health-checklist.xlsx (actionable items).

Thanks,

--
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Product Ops Manager

stephanie@redwood.ai

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Ben Harris <ben.harris@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private release: safety raft & undo protocol — proposed cadence and windows

Stephanie — thanks for the clear proposal. Quick notes inline and a couple technical caveats.

On KV-cache warmup / drain timing:
> - KV cache warmup script as part of post-deploy hook.

We should avoid a post-deploy full warmup for the broad roll until we see canary latency stable for at least 45m. Warmup increases load spikes; instead, recommend: mirror 10% for 2h (as you suggested), then run a staged warmup to only the new pool with rate-limited prefetch (ramp 10% -> 50% over 20m).

Pin TTL: 72h auto-unpin is fine as default but add a manual shelf/extend path for customers who require longer pins (Doc: /undo-protocol/spec-v1 has a manual shelving section).

Orchestrator constraints: the orchestrator's live-eviction window currently holds KV range locks for up to 15m during node reimages. For the staged rollback lane, we should allocate a 30m buffer in the runbook to allow KV rebalancing.

Circuit-breaker metrics: recommend adding a token-throttle-fraction metric (observed in last incident) to the gating list.

I'll add small edits to the attached PDF with the updated timing windows and buffer margins.

- Dev

Thanks — a couple calendar/ops constraints from Acme side:

- Acme DB team has an existing maintenance window Tue 03:00-04:30 local; canary should avoid overlap with their longest locks. Can we shift canary to start at 01:30 and run through 04:00 with a hard stop at 04:00?
- Oncall coverage: we need coverage from the Platform oncall for both nights (canary + broad). Can Dev or someone from runtime add the oncall Slack bridge to the runbook?
- Network approvals: Ben, we need the list of firewall approvers and a named network contact (NOC) so we can add them to the maintenance ticket.

Also: add a short acceptance test for the canary — a scripted sampling of 50 requests against a pinned model variant with token counts representative of Acme's bursts. If that passes at 95th latency < X ms, we proceed; else we initiate staged rollback.

I can block the windows on Acme's calendar after we have written signoff.

Laura
